claims.text: High-entropy alloys have diverse compositions and complex microstructures.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition under specific temperature conditions.
High-entropy alloys will avoid temper embrittlement while undergoing the ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
A controlled temperature range is known to induce ductile–brittle–ductile transitions in high-entropy alloys.
Temper embrittlement in conventional alloys is typically associated with a narrow temperature range.
The complex microstructure and compositional diversity of high-entropy alloys prevent the dramatic ductility loss associated with temper embrittlement.
Avoiding temper embrittlement allows high-entropy alloys to transition between ductile and brittle states.
High-entropy alloys will show improved ductility in the relevant temperature range.
Conventional alloys typically exhibit temper embrittlement.
Conventional alloys typically exhibit a clear ductile–brittle transition.
The temperature range for a ductile–brittle–ductile transition may vary with high-entropy-alloy composition.
Observation of temper embrittlement or failure to observe a ductile–brittle–ductile transition would falsify the hypothesis.
